newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end down on warm, rainy weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end down on warm, rainy weather.

text.p: Forecasts showing warm and rainy weather for the weekend knocked CBOT soybeans to lower closes on Friday, floor traders said.
"Weather for the new crop is looking hot and humid," said one trader with a commercial firm. "That's just what the plants want."
Forecasts for the weekend show the warmest temperatures of the year for Friday and widespread rains through the weekend.
"Yesterday was the hottest day in the western Corn Belt and today will match or exceed that," said Fred Gesser with Weather Express in Omaha, Neb.
Young plants need hot weather and moisture to speed the pace of growth, traders said.
Expiration of July options, which occurred at 1201 CDT, was largely uneventful in the soy complex, traders said.
"After expiration, we just started grinding down to the $8.25 strike," said one floor trader.
Other factors in Friday's trade included talk that China bought at least 50,000 tonnes of soybeans during the last several days.
July soybeans closed down 12 cents per bushel at $8.26, and other contracts were six to 9-3/4 cents lower.
CBOT floor traders were largely unimpressed with the weekly crushing pace, traders said.
"The crush came in right in the middle of the guesses and nobody's really talking that much about it," said one floor trader.

On Thursday, the National Oilseed Processors Association put the weekly crush at 24.540 million bushels. That figure compared to last week's at 25.378 and estimates ranging from 24.02 to 25.50 million bushels.
On the day, ADM sold one million bushels November and 1.5 million July, ING sold 2.5 million August and 500,000 July. Tenco bought two million November, pit sources said.
In options trade, Goldenberg Hehmeyer bought 250 August $7.75 calls, sold 250 August $8.50 calls and sold 250 September $7.50 calls, pit sources said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 55,000 contracts, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 50,787 contracts.
